terms.meaning: a library that reads text from PDF files
optical character recognition, reading text from images of pages
a text pattern used to find labels or phrases
a set of named values, such as a project name and a page count

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Module setup
sections.what: Loads the PDF reader, the file path helper, the type labels and the pattern-matching tool.
sections.why: Needed to read PDFs and search their text.

sections.name: parse_rfp (part 1)
sections.title: Reading the PDF and the file-name project name
sections.what: Checks the file exists, reads text from every page into one block, and takes a starting project name from the file name with RFP suffixes removed.
sections.why: Likely reason: a page that fails is skipped with a warning so one bad page does not stop the whole read.
sections.watch_out: A PDF with no extractable text raises an error that is re-wrapped with a general message.

sections.name: parse_rfp (part 2)
sections.title: Finding a project name inside the text
sections.what: Searches the text for labels such as Project Name, Project or Client, and uses the first short match as the project name. It then returns the text, name, page count and path together.
sections.why: Likely reason: a name written in the document is usually more accurate than the file name.
sections.watch_out: The plain Project label can match ordinary phrases, which then become the project name.

sections.name: extract_text_from_pdf
sections.title: Text-only helper
sections.what: Returns only the full text of a PDF by calling the main reader and keeping that part.
sections.why: Likely reason: a convenience for callers that need only the text.

summary: Reads an RFP PDF, extracts all its text, and works out a project name from the file name or from labels in the text.
purpose: Turn an uploaded RFP PDF into plain text and basic details for the rest of the pipeline.
why: The module docstring says it parses RFP PDFs and extracts text, which is the input for matching and generation.
how: Open the PDF, read each page's text, and stop with an error if nothing is found. Take a starting project name from the file name, then look for labels such as Project Name or Client in the text and use the first short match.
inputs: Path to a PDF file and a verbose flag.
outputs: A dictionary with the full text, project name, page count and file path. The helper function returns only the text.
risks: Image-only (scanned) PDFs produce an error because no OCR is used. The label search can match ordinary phrases such as project management. A missing file raises an error.
debug: If the error says no text, open the PDF to check whether it is scanned. If the project name is wrong, compare the label patterns with the document wording.
